A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same JiT research work, with 18 complete pages including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the equations, figures, tables, and appendices are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy experiments, ImageNet generation results, architectural ablations, and additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and generated examples, including the JiT results in Tables 2–6 and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The JiT architecture, x-prediction with v-loss, training and sampling algorithms, and optional architectural components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic experiment and ImageNet tasks, including generation at resolutions 64, 256, 512, and 1024 and the retained appendix experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. ADM-G and RIN remain in Tables 7 and 8; their revised numerical entries do not introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Table 7 revises reported baseline model sizes for ImageNet 256×256: ADM-G changes from 559M to 554M parameters and RIN from 320M to 410M. These are changes to the reported comparison settings, without evidence that experiments were rerun. Other protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The prediction/loss, noise-level, bottleneck, architectural, and guidance analyses are unchanged. Appendix B retains identical training-loss, pre-conditioning, classification-loss, and cross-resolution analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, explicit seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: In Table 7, ADM-G FID/IS changes from 7.72/172.7 to 4.59/186.7, and RIN from 3.95/216.0 to 3.42/182.0. RIN now ranks ahead of JiT-B/16, whose FID remains 3.66. These are revised reference entries, with changed reported model sizes; all JiT results and appendix findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The manifold assumption, prediction-space transformations, loss derivations, Equations 1–8, and Appendix B.2 pre-conditioner formulation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about clean-data prediction, limited network capacity, and self-contained pixel-space generation with plain Transformers.

C2.justification: The explanations of prediction failures, bottleneck benefits, overfitting, cross-resolution behavior, and potential applicability to other domains are unchanged. No limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 9 retain identical implementation, optimization, training, EMA, guidance, sampling, and evaluation details. Code references and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to previous diffusion and manifold-learning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 17 November 2025 to v2 dated 7 January 2026. Body prose, terminology, headings, and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, and page layout are unchanged, including all appendix sample grids. Table 7 changes only numerical cells.

improvement.justification: The Table 7 updates may correct a copying error: v1 repeated the ADM-G and RIN parameter counts and FID/IS values from the 512×512 comparison in Table 8. However, neither PDF explains or substantiates the replacement values, so improved accuracy cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence. With the method, original experiments, and appendices unchanged, the net quality benefit remains uncertain.
